There is a concrete example worth separating from speculation: in two-dimensional SU(2) YM, the genus enters the representation sum, and the zero-area partition function becomes \(\zeta(2g-2)\). That is an exact topology–zeta connection. For our present four-dimensional source law, though, changing a finite spatial topology while retaining a simple loop leaves the local norm obstruction in place.

A change of observables gives another concrete lead. Using SU(2) representation characters, winding can be accompanied by a character factor that makes the operation isometric in the Haar norm and uniformly bounded in our finite YM norm. This fixes one defect of the earlier winding operators. It does not yet give the Weil pairing, but it is a more specific next step than changing the spatial topology alone.

The most useful distinction is whether a proposed change can alter both required features: logarithmic growth at high frequency and the exact prime-power correlations. I’m recording the character-operator calculation alongside the topology options. I also checked that modular-surface scattering contains a completed-zeta ratio, giving a concrete comparison for the separate transfer-function objective, with no established YM pairing identity.

**Yes—if the change produces new observable relations or a different source domain.** Changing the finite spatial topology alone will not rescue the source law we just tested.

Its obstruction was
\[
\|Jf\|^2\le C_I\|f\|_2^2
\]
for inputs supported in a fixed interval \(I\). The proof did not use the loop’s contractibility. A simple loop around a new handle or noncontractible cycle therefore encounters the same obstruction under the stated finite-state assumptions.

I see five worthwhile directions.

1. **Replace fundamental-holonomy powers with representation characters.**

   This gives a concrete improvement within our existing YM model. Let \(\chi_n\) be the SU(2) character of the representation of dimension \(n\), and define
   \[
   (V_nF)(g)=\chi_n(g)F(g^n).
   \]
   Then
   \[
   V_n\chi_m=\chi_{nm},\qquad V_nV_k=V_{nk}.
   \]
   These operations are isometries in the Haar class-function norm and uniformly bounded in our actual finite YM norm. Thus multiplicative arithmetic now acts through **bounded Hilbert-space operators**, improving on the earlier winding operations.

   The simplest Mellin source built from these characters still fails the growth test. Nevertheless, this is a better algebra in which to investigate additional insertions and identities for the actual mixed pairing.

2. **Use topology in a setting where its effect is exactly calculable.**

   Two-dimensional SU(2) YM provides a striking example. In the standard character normalization, its zero-area partition function on a closed genus-\(g\) surface is
   \[
   Z_g(0)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^{2-2g}=\zeta(2g-2),\qquad g\ge2.
   \]
   Here topology supplies the exponent and representation dimensions supply the integers. This is an established topology–zeta connection. [Runkel–Szegedy, Remark 5.8](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00220-020-03902-1)

   I would use this as a controlled comparison for surface gluing and boundary observables. It changes our four-dimensional theory, and these special partition-function values do not yet supply the Weil mixed pairing. Analytically continuing genus also does not automatically preserve a physical positive norm.

3. **Introduce arithmetic geometry with a scattering boundary.**

   The modular surface \(PSL(2,\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathbb H\) has the exact scattering coefficient
   \[
   C(s)=\frac{\Lambda(2s-1)}{\Lambda(2s)},\qquad
   \Lambda(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s).
   \]
   This makes it a concrete comparison for our shifted-transfer objective. The arithmetic quotient and metric matter beyond the surface’s topological type. [Levitin–Strohmaier, §7.3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1812.05554)

   However, physical scattering unitarity does not force the relevant resonances onto the RH line. An adelic construction addresses the prime contributions more directly, but its trace-formula and positivity obligations remain substantial. [Connes](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9811068)

4. **Allow genuinely singular or collective observables.**

   Renormalized field insertions, infinitely many distinct contours, or controlled continuum limits could escape the local \(L^2\) bound. A finite collection of bounded modifications cannot.

   There is a useful precise restriction: **a limit of pairings with a uniform local \(L^2\) bound retains that bound.** Any successful limiting construction must therefore lose this uniformity while retaining a well-defined positive pairing. Merely choosing a stronger topology on the test space does not change an existing pairing.

5. **Change the flux or defect sector.**

   Magnetic disorder lines, boundary degrees of freedom, or different global gauge groups genuinely enlarge the observable structure. Wilson–’t Hooft operators supply electric and magnetic labels. [Kapustin](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0501015)

   The strongest established connection to Hecke operations uses twisted **\(N=4\) supersymmetric YM** compactified on a Riemann surface. That is a substantial model change, and its geometric correspondence still needs a compatible positive source metric for our purpose. [Kapustin–Witten](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0604151)

**My recommendation:** pursue the character operations first within the current model, and use two-dimensional YM as the topology comparison. Each candidate must explain both the logarithmic high-frequency growth and the exact correlations at prime-power logarithmic separations.
